title: "Trouble Everywhere I Go" and "Murder's Going to Be My Crime"
summary: She explains the Houston good-time house behind one song and the jealous meaning of another.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: You must have been plenty sad when you sang that song "Trouble Everywhere I Go."

Well, I'll tell you, at home in Houston, my sister had a good time house, used to have a lot of girls -- we had a lot ______ and a lot of girls used to come around our house and we used to play cards and they used to drink ______ and talk and drink and you know, dance and carry on like that thing and everytime you'd turn around, the law was coming there ______ and I would get so mad, I'd say, "How come the law keeps coming to Lucy's house?" You know. But (unintelligible) when I was living in Chicago, I say everytime, everywhere I go, it seemed like trouble is there. I wanted to live at my sister's, but I couldn't live there because the law coming and I'm scared of policemen. Always has been. And I say, I told Lucy, I say, "I ain't got no enemies." Lucy say, "Sippie, you got to have enemies. People can just don't like you, period. You don't have to do nothing and people will ______ you." That's
That song "Murder ________ Crime," what did you mean by that?

I mean (unintelligible) I ain't going to steal nothing from you, but I'm liable to kill you if you do something to me. Say (unintelligible), but "Murder's going to be my crime, because if you don't change your mind, I'm going to end up killing you. (Singing) is my crime. (Unintelligible) something about I'm going to kill you (unintelligible) I'm going to kill you and murder's going to be my crime. I ain't going to be charged with stealing, because I'm going to kill somebody. See, when I catch you with a woman.

I had another song (unintelligible). I'm going to build me a mansion way up on ________ hill where I can go up there and drink all the whiskey I want, honey, right from the still. Then it goes on and say, If you take my baby, you sure ________ because I got a new way of loving that's really ________. (Inaudible).
What's the new way of living that ________?
I ain't going to tell you.
Oh no? Why not? I want to know that secret.
Well, how am I going to get smart if I can't learn it from you?
I ain't going to tell you my secret. You find a way. You find a way.
If I tell you my secret, then that'll be your secret. (Unintelligible) have a secret, everybody's secret. That's the way it is.
